headline: AI migrated legacy COBOL programs to Java, bugs and all
summary: The AI-powered migration process successfully converted the code, but also faithfully reproduced existing bugs, highlighting the challenges of automated legacy system modernization.
details: An artificial intelligence system successfully undertook the task of migrating legacy COBOL programs to Java. This process involved translating the older, established codebase into a more modern programming language.

A notable outcome of this automated migration was the transfer of existing bugs from the original COBOL code into the newly generated Java programs. This highlights the complexities and challenges inherent in fully automating the modernization of legacy systems.

headline_marked: [[Stop Prompt Engineering, Start Context Engineering]] for better AI agent results
headline: Stop Prompt Engineering, Start Context Engineering for better AI agent results
summary: Learn how to build effective AI agents by shifting focus from prompt engineering to context engineering, ensuring consistent results with simple prompts.
details: AI agents are often discussed abstractly. This guide provides a practical breakdown of what makes an agent work, including a simple example for clarity.
An agent is defined as an LLM (brain) combined with a Loop, Tools, and Context. The 'harness' (like Claude Code or Cowork) is simply the application that executes this operational loop.
The core shift is from traditional prompt engineering to context engineering. Rich, well-structured context is key to transforming a brief prompt into a high-quality result.
The process follows a consistent structure: context, memory, and tools are set up once. This initial setup then allows for simple prompts to yield consistent and reliable outcomes.
This approach prioritizes front-loading comprehensive context upfront, rather than constantly refining prompts. This ensures that every subsequent request can remain straightforward and effective.
Utilizing templates can further streamline this process. They enable quick responses to FAQs and efficient storage of reusable information snippets.
